The following theorem shows that majorized parameter vector of one set of random variables implies greater maximum order statistic than the other, in term of usual stochastic ordering. Theorem 3.1 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Xi and Yi be two sets of mutually independent random variables each satisfying Poisson distribution with parameters µi and µ∗i respectively. quote: [Section 3.2 preamble:] Let X1, X2, . . . , Xn be a sequence of random variables satisfying geometric distribution with parameter q1, q2, . . . , qn. Now, if F̄1:n(u) and Fn:n(u) be the survival function and distribution functions of X1:n and Xn:n respectively, then, for all u = 0, 1, 2, . . ., F̄1:n(u) = Π_{i=1}^n qi^{u+1} and Fn:n(u) = Π_{k=1}^n (1 − qk^{u+1}). Now, if r1:n(u) denotes hazard rate function of the random variable X1:n, then, for all u = 0, 1, 2, . . ., it can be written that, r1:n(u) = [F̄1:n(u) − F̄1:n(u + 1)] / F̄1:n(u) = 1 − Π_{i=1}^n qi^{u+1} / Π_{i=1}^n qi^u = 1 − Π_{i=1}^n qi. Let, X1, X2, . . . , Xn and X1∗, X2∗, . . . , Xn∗ be two sets of random variables following geometric distribution having parameters q1, q2, . . . , qn and q1∗, q2∗, . . . , qn∗ respectively. Also let, q = (q1, q2, . . . , qn) and q∗ = (q1∗, q2∗, . . . , qn∗). The following theorem shows that, under certain condition X1:n is greater than Y1:n in hazard rate ordering. The proof is straight forward and hence omitted. Theorem 3.3 For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Xi and Yi be two sets of mutually independent random variables each satisfying geometric distribution with parameters qi and qi∗ respectively. Then Π_{i=1}^n qi ≥ Π_{i=1}^n qi∗ implies X1:n ≥hr Y1:n.
